dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Wilson disease

Progressive bilateral caudate and putaminal necrosis, symmetric rigidity with pyramidal signs (brisk reflexes), postural instability, and bulbar symptoms in a young patient, with elevated CSF protein and no inflammatory markers, is highly characteristic of Wilson disease causing hepatic metabolic failure with copper deposition and necrosis in the basal ganglia.

Hepatic Wilson disease (without prominent neurological manifestation)

Mitochondrial encephalopathy (e.g., Leigh syndrome)

Toxic/metabolic basal ganglia necrosis (e.g., carbon monoxide or cyanide exposure)
